newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt on nationwide "protect antiquities" sweep.
newsitem.headline: Egypt on nationwide "protect antiquities" sweep.

text.p: Egyptian police caught more than 100 alleged swindlers, pick-pockets, unlicensed tour guides and souvenir sellers as part of nationwide campaign to protect the country's antiquities, officials said on Friday.

The government press said the police raided archeological sites in Cairo and the southern resorts of Luxor and Aswan and caught two men who were trying to smuggle 46 invaluable statues and a cache of stones.
"It's a purification campaign, we're trying to nip any illegal activities in the bud," one official who asked not to be named told Reuters.

The Interior Ministry and the Supreme Council for Antiquities (SCA) are behind the campaign and police are currently interrogating several people, including a British archeologist, for allegedly stealing antiquities.
Experts say that the police in their zealous campaign have mistaken several antique objects for antiquities, but Cairo newspapers have been less discerning.
On Thursday, they reported police had raided the house of a wood trader in a posh Cairo residential area and found a cache of "antiquities", including several colonial French columns.

Earlier, the papers said police had issued a warrant to search the library of British archeologist Fernand Debono on suspicion he was hiding ancient manuscripts. Debono says the books in question date back to the early 1800s.
"I am not a dealer, I am an archeologist and a well-known one. I bought these books from a trader and didn't think I had to declare them," a distraught Debono told Reuters.

Ali Hassan, the newly-appointed chairman of SCA, has also ordered a review of foreign archeological missions excavating in Egypt. The state's attorney general also went to London this week to search for stolen antiquities there.
